title: Specify the clustering objective before adding weights
status: Corrected formulation or classical result with an explicit worked example
summary: T=W+B. For nonnegative a,b with a+b>0, maximizing aB−bW over the same partitions gives exactly the minimizers of W. definitions: A partition consists of nonempty clusters C_j, sizes n_j and centroids μ_j. The global centroid is μ.

These definitions apply to a fixed dataset and fixed Euclidean metric. An objective also needs a direction of optimization, admissible partitions and explicit weights.

status: Corrected formulation or classical result with an explicit worked example
summary: The solutions are componentwise soft threshold x_i=sign(z_i)max(|z_i|−λ,0), radial shrink x=max(1−λ/||z||₂,0)z, and ridge x=z/(1+λ), respectively. result.statement: The solutions are componentwise soft threshold x_i=sign(z_i)max(|z_i|−λ,0), radial shrink x=max(1−λ/||z||₂,0)z, and ridge x=z/(1+λ), respectively.
result.proof: For ℓ₁ the coordinates separate. At a positive coordinate, optimality gives x_i−z_i+λ=0; at a negative one it gives x_i−z_i−λ=0. At zero, the subgradient interval [−λ,λ] contains z_i exactly when |z_i|≤λ. For the unsquared ℓ₂ norm and a nonzero solution, x−z+λx/||x||=0, so x points along z and its length is ||z||−λ. At zero, optimality requires z in the radius-λ Euclidean ball, giving the threshold case. Ridge is differentiable everywhere: x−z+λx=0. These conditions are sufficient by convexity and unique by strict convexity of the full objective.

example.conclusion: Writing ||M||₂ without stating whether M is a vector or a matrix is incomplete: a matrix spectral norm, Frobenius norm and entrywise norm lead to different optimization problems.

result.statement: For any group, the transformed plaquette isP′=g₁Pg₁⁻¹. ForZ₂ it is exactlyP. The sixteen four-edge configurations split into two gauge orbits of eight, classified by their plaquette sign.
result.proof: Multiply transformed edges in loop order. Every adjacentg_j⁻¹g_j cancels, leaving only conjugation at the base vertex. Trace is cyclic, so its value is unchanged. For the finite model, each of four vertex signs appears twice in the product and squares to one, provingP′=P. There are sixteen gauge assignments, but the all-negative assignment acts trivially just like the all-positive assignment. The action therefore has an effective group of size eight. If a gauge assignment fixes every edge, connectedness forces all its vertex signs equal, so this is the entire stabilizer and every orbit has size eight. Eight configurations have each product sign, completing the classification.
